title: A table can draw a rule between its body rows
body:
`Block::Table { header, rows }` in `src/lib.rs` holds a table's header cells and its body rows. The `table` function draws the header, then a rule of `─` runs joined by `─┼─` at the column widths, then each body row. A body row whose cells wrap takes several lines, and nothing marks where one row ends and the next begins.

## Proposal

- `Block::Table` gains `rules: bool`. When it is set, `table` draws the header rule again after each body row but the last.
- `parse` sets `rules` to false, so the output of `render` and `text` does not change. A caller that lays blocks out itself sets the flag on the block before `layout`, as with `wrap` on `Block::Code`.
- `stacked` ignores the flag. It already puts a blank line between records.

## Rejected

- An argument to `layout`. It would apply to every table in the call, and coax chooses per table.
- Drawing rules only when a body row wraps. Jack wants the caller to choose, with nothing automatic.

## Cost

- A new field on a public enum variant breaks code that builds `Block::Table`, or matches it without `..`. The next release moves the minor.
